mutants.reason: funct7 test inverted: a genuine DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU (funct7=0000001) is never decoded, so no pcpi_wait or pcpi_ready/pcpi_wr is produced and the instruction times out; other funct7 values would be wrongly accepted.
Whole decode condition negated: valid division instructions are not recognised, and in idle or reset cycles the decode case fires on arbitrary pcpi_insn funct3 bits, giving spurious pcpi_wait/ready.

Quotient sign condition inverted (== instead of !=): DIV results with opposite-sign operands lose the negation and same-sign ones are wrongly negated, including the 0x80000000/-1 overflow case. Divide by zero is unchanged because |rs2 is 0.
instr_div && instr_rem is never true, so a negative divisor is never negated for signed DIV/REM. A negative rs2 then gives a wrong quotient and remainder (for example 7 / -2, and -2^31 / -1).

Operator precedence change: with resetn && pcpi_valid true, the instruction-type check is bypassed and the !pcpi_ready guard is ignored. The funct3 case then decodes non-DIV instructions, and decode retriggers on the cycle pcpi_ready is high, causing a spurious second wait/ready pulse.
Opcode test inverted: the OP opcode 0110011 is no longer decoded, so real division instructions are never accepted and no wait/ready occurs. Non-OP opcodes with funct7=1 would be wrongly accepted.

The restoring-division compare is inverted: the divisor is subtracted when it is larger than the dividend, so quotient and remainder are wrong for essentially all divisions, including division by zero.

|| became &&: instr_div and instr_rem are never both set, so outsign is always 0. Negative quotients are not negated, and REM with a negative dividend returns the wrong sign (and wrong value on divide by zero).
Precedence change makes outsign=1 whenever rs2 is nonzero, for any instruction type. Same-sign DIV, DIVU and REMU results are wrongly negated, and REM with a positive dividend gets the wrong sign.
Completion condition inverted: pcpi_ready/pcpi_wr are not issued when the quotient mask reaches zero and are issued at the wrong time. Results are wrong and completion is missing, early or spurious.

instr_div && instr_rem is never true, so a negative dividend is never negated for signed DIV/REM. A negative rs1 gives a wrong quotient and remainder, including the divide-by-zero remainder and the overflow case.

pcpi_wait <= any || resetn holds pcpi_wait high whenever resetn=1, even when idle. This also triggers a spurious start, so a pcpi_ready/pcpi_wr pulse appears with no instruction outstanding, and pcpi_wait is no longer 0 when idle.
